canonical_data: project folders of generated output and assets plus a local database of projects, conversations, messages, runs, and agent sessions
current_repo_note: Four months old at review with the highest adoption in the queue. Its daemon spawns and supervises the host agents itself, so the reserved add-on question does not apply. The licence file is a silently modified Apache text: one clause in the redistribution section is shortened and the warranty section is retitled; the platform still detects the standard licence. Packaged beta builds bundle a closed third-party command-line tool.
strengths: The adapter layer is a data contract, so many vendors' agent tools are driven by one generic engine
A tool-loop guard and run-failure classification give the wrapper its own failure semantics instead of streaming a stuck agent forever
Test volume in the daemon exceeds its implementation, and browser suites run on every change
weaknesses: The licence text is a silently modified Apache licence, and packaged beta builds bundle an unlicensed third-party tool
A single composition file of nearly seventeen thousand lines holds the process-spawn path alongside everything else
A safety-telemetry channel that the analytics toggle cannot disable, and a readme that leads with a paid model service
why_it_matters: The most adopted example of a workflow layer that owns its own daemon, persistence, and process supervision around whichever coding agent the user already runs.
